_doc: Scoped corridors view for gojek Bite-2 economics cascade

_fare_record.source: No scheduled per-seat premium boat transfer Labuan Bajo->Sumba. Budget floor = Pelni car ferry ~24h, IDR 244k (~$15) incl berth+3 meals (FB group, each way). Premium = NIHI private boat charters (whole-boat, luxury) or fly. Modeled premium per-seat for a fast luxury-resort sea transfer ~$200 (between $15 slow-ferry and whole-boat charter, scaled to Nihi-class clientele on a 90nm open-water crossing).
_fare_record.anchor_rationale: Ultra-luxury resort corridor (NIHI). Currently no per-seat premium sea transfer; clientele flies or charters whole boats. Modeled per-seat anchor avoids both under-claim (slow Pelni) and over-claim (whole-boat charter). Greenfield-thin (R5).

_demand_record.source: Ultra-niche: NIHI ~30 villas, guests overwhelmingly arrive by air/charter flight, not by sea. No published Labuan Bajo->Sumba passenger crossing count. NULL beats a guess (R2). Tiny pool even if modeled.

_fare_record.source: No direct premium fast ferry on the 150nm crossing. Substitute premium point-to-point mode = flight Lombok(LOP)->Labuan Bajo(LBJ): IDR 1.5-2.5M ($100-170) one-way (Garuda/Wings/Lion, surfwells 2026). Pelni slow ferry IDR 236k ($27), 24-36h = budget floor. Liveaboard 4D3N $200-1000/pax = bundled cruise, excluded as overclaim. Modeled premium per-seat transfer anchored at air-fare midpoint ~$130.
_fare_record.anchor_rationale: Navier Quanta-LR = fast point-to-point sea transfer; currently the only fast P2P option on this corridor is the FLIGHT, so the relevant traveler-paid comparable is the airfare, not the multi-day liveaboard. R5 greenfield-thin signal.

_demand_record.source: No published ridership for a direct Lombok->Labuan Bajo crossing because none operates as a scheduled fast route. Labuan Bajo arrivals are dominated by air + Bali-origin liveaboards (R3: destination arrivals != this crossing). NULL beats a guess.

_fare_record.source: Premium private transfer tier, Sanur->Nusa Penida. Tripadvisor 'Private and Luxury' $75/adult (bundles tour, excluded as overclaim); Klook Premium Speedboat; standard fast boat $37-40. Anchored at $60 = clean premium point-to-point transfer, conservative vs $75 bundled.
_fare_record.anchor_rationale: Navier = premium private on-demand boat sold per-seat. Comparable = premium transfer tier, NOT budget ferry (under-claim) and NOT whole-boat charter (over-claim). Market parity, win on product.

_demand_record.source: Klungkung Tourism Office (Dispar) official levy count, 2025: 1,078,125 visitors to Kawasan Wisata Nusa Penida (1,070,616 adults @ Rp25,000 retribution + 7,509 children @ Rp15,000), PAD Rp 26.88B (NusaBali, 27-Feb-2026, https://www.nusabali.com/berita/214419/tahun-2025-nusa-penida-dikunjungi-1-juta-lebih-wisatawan). 2023 was ~729k (Klungkung); regent's 2026 target 2-2.5M. Levy is collected at island entry -> fee-paying turnstile-grade count (R3-GOLD pattern). Nusa Penida district (incl. Lembongan/Ceningan) is boat-only - no airport, no bridge to Bali -> R3-EXCEPTION: arrivals = crossing ridership.
_demand_record.method: 1,078,125 visitors x2 = 2,156,250 one-way fast-boat crossings (all origins). Origin split haircut: Sanur is the dominant fast-boat gateway, Kusamba + Padangbai secondary -> Benoa/Sanur share modeled 0.70 -> 1,509,375 ~= 1,500,000 one-way. Conservative: levy likely undercounts Lembongan-only day-trippers who can bypass the Penida levy point.

_fare_record.source: Premium transfer tier, Bali->Gili Trawangan. Tripadvisor 'Luxury Speedboat Transfer' $64; standard $28-42; budget ~$20; whole-boat private $500-1200.
_fare_record.anchor_rationale: Premium transfer tier, per-seat. Market parity, win on product.

_demand_record.source: No published count for the Bali-origin fast-boat leg specifically. Triangulation anchors: (1) UPTD Pelabuhan Bangsal (Lombok-side public port) recorded 574,107 arrivals to Gili Trawangan (406k) + Gili Air (168k) in 2024 - BPK-audited figure exposing Dispar undercount of 128,774 (Radar Lombok, Aug-2025, https://radarlombok.co.id/bpk-temukan-selisih-besar-data-kunjungan-wisata-gili-pad-berpotensi-bocor-banyak.html) - that is the LOMBOK leg (R3-PIER: different pier), used as magnitude bound; (2) Kab. Lombok Utara 2024 total visitors ~700k (ekbisntb.com, Jan-2025); (3) live operator schedules: daily fast-boat departures from Padangbai, Sanur, Serangan and Amed by Eka Jaya (180 seats, multiple trips/day), BlueWater Express (3x daily peak), Gili Getaway, Semaya One, Wanderlust, Ostina etc. (gilitickets.com, ferryhopper.com, 2025-26 listings).
_demand_record.method: R4 freq x capacity for the Bali-origin leg: ~12 fast-boat sailings/day/direction x ~140 avg seats x 0.55 load x 365 x 2 directions = ~674k; mid-point with seasonality (Nov-Mar monsoon cancellations) -> 600,000 one-way/yr. Gilis are boat-only (R3-EXCEPTION on access mode) but the pool is split between the Bali leg (this corridor) and the Bangsal/Lombok leg - the two legs are kept separate to avoid double-count. Tag T5/modeled; the 574k audited Lombok-side figure says total-island magnitude supports this comfortably.

_fare_record.source: No scheduled per-seat passenger service runs directly between the inner and outer rings; inter-island hopping is done by charter/private-tour boats. Modeled by distance interpolation on the observed Marina Ancol tariff curve (10nm Rp155k -> 35nm Rp335k); 22nm => ~Rp270,000.
_fare_record.method: R5/R14 operating-thin/greenfield: no direct premium per-seat product to observe on this inter-ring leg => modeled fare. Interpolated premium per-seat ~Rp270k. Flag to parent cascade.

_demand_record.source: No published count for inter-ring (inner->outer) crossings. Visitors transit mainland<->island; scheduled inner-to-outer island-hopping service does not exist as a counted route.
_demand_record.method: R2 (null beats guess) + R5/R14: no scheduled inter-ring service, uncounted island-hopping subset => demand NULL. Route to cascade.

_fare_record.currency_basis: IDR converted @ ~16,300 IDR/USD (2025 avg; fares are 2024-25 listings)
_fare_record.source: Official Marina Ancol speedboat tariff table (pulauseribu-resorts.com / visitpulauseribu.co.id): Ayer/Bidadari Rp155,000 one-way regular speedboat; budget wooden boat ex-Kaliadem Rp90-110k; private speedboat charter Rp2,400,000/boat (Ayer/Bidadari/Kelor-Onrust) => ~Rp200-300k/seat. Premium per-seat anchored at ~Rp190,000.
_fare_record.method: Fare ladder: budget wooden boat ~Rp110k / standard speedboat Rp155k / PREMIUM private-speedboat-per-seat ~Rp190k (ANCHOR) / whole-boat charter Rp2.4M. Picked premium per-seat (R1, R1-RESORT). Short 10nm crossing; speedboat is the premium-vs-wooden-boat product.

_demand_record.source: Sudin Parekraf Kepulauan Seribu official 2025 category breakdown (via pulauseribu.jakarta.go.id, 11-Jan-2026): total 398,519 visitors (2024: 411,161); resort islands 13,932 (TOP = Bidadari #1, then Putri, Macan); tourism islands 3,575; nature-reserve islands 537. Inner-ring = Bidadari+Ayer resort share (~half of resort pool, Bidadari is #1) + Onrust/Cipir/Kelor historical-park day-trips (pulau wisata/cagar) => ~10,000/yr.
_demand_record.method: R3 APPLIED (critical): the 398,519 headline is dominated by RESIDENTIAL budget islands (380,475 = 96%, Pari/Untung-Jawa/Tidung) reached by separate cheap-ferry crossings, NOT this premium resort/historical corridor. On-corridor pool = resort+wisata+cagar islands only (~18k total), of which inner-ring (Bidadari/Ayer/Onrust) modeled at ~10k. Kepulauan Seribu is boat-only (R3-EXCEPTION: arrivals=crossing ridership) but the residential-island majority is off-corridor, so headline is NOT used. Allocation across rings is modeled => med confidence.

_fare_record.currency_basis: IDR converted @ ~16,300 IDR/USD (2025 avg; fares are 2024-25 listings)
_fare_record.source: Official Marina Ancol tariff table: Pelangi/Sepa/Macan & Kotok/Putri Rp335,000 one-way regular speedboat; Pulau Pantara Rp455,000 one-way; Tokopedia (endangeredstore) Pelangi/Sepa one-way Rp340,000. Resort day/2D1N packages (Sepa Rp1,250,000 one-day incl. transport+lunch+activities; Putri 2D1N Rp1,610,000-2,200,000) include premium boat but are bundles, not pure transfer. Premium per-seat transfer anchored ~Rp400,000.
_fare_record.method: Fare ladder (resort-only, no budget wooden boat to outer resorts): standard speedboat Rp335k / PREMIUM resort speedboat ~Rp400k (ANCHOR, between Rp335k std and Rp455k Pantara) / Pantara Rp455k / whole-boat charter (over-claim, excluded). Picked premium per-seat (R1, R1-RESORT). 35nm resort transfer.

_demand_record.source: Sudin Parekraf Kepulauan Seribu official 2025: resort islands 13,932 total (Putri #2 and Macan #3 most-visited resorts; plus Pelangi/Sepa/Pantara). Outer-ring resort share modeled at ~7,000/yr (remainder of the 13,932 resort pool after inner-ring Bidadari/Ayer).
_demand_record.method: R3 APPLIED: headline 398,519 excluded (96% off-corridor residential islands). On-corridor outer-ring = resort islands Putri/Macan/Pelangi/Sepa/Pantara, ~7k/yr (resort pool 13,932 minus inner-ring share). Boat-only (R3-EXCEPTION) but premium-resort subset only. Allocation modeled => med confidence.

NO commuter ferry exists East Coast->Marina/CBD — road commute only (ECP). Singapore River taxi (Marina<->Robertson Quay) is intra-river at S$3-7 (commuter single-class, no premium tier; R5-EXT). Harbour water-taxi is whole-boat charter S$80-130/trip (overclaim). Modeled premium per-seat commute fare anchored at road/Grab parity East Coast->CBD ~S$24 = ~$18.
_fare_record.method: modeled — greenfield commute, road-parity (R14a greenfield + R5-EXT single-class commute)

_demand_record.gross_pool_basis: SingStat Census of Population 2020 (data.gov.sg dataset d_5b38192e9c6f8d2c5f38c70939c76e71): 50,621 employed residents of the EAST REGION work in the Downtown Core planning area (of 280,589 total Downtown Core workers). Annualized commute trips: 50,621 workers x 2 one-way trips/day x 220 working days = ~22.3M one-way trips/yr. Marine Parade (Central Region) coastal residents are additional but not counted (conservative).

sources.label: SingStat Census 2020 - Employed residents by planning area of workplace x region of residence (Downtown Core row: Total 280,589; East Region 50,621)
SingStat Census 2020 Key Findings - 284k residents (12.9% of workforce) work in Downtown Core

_demand_record.haircut_rationale: R3-LAND tension flagged explicitly: 100% of these trips are made by road/MRT today - there is NO current water commute, so this is a substitution-share model, not observed ridership (same structure that was NULLed for Dubai-Sharjah; retained here per parent instruction because the corridor has dedicated endpoints in dense waterfront catchments). Addressable 0.5% = coastal-strip catchment (~1/3 of East Region Downtown Core workers live within reach of an East Coast jetty) x ~1.5% premium water-commute mode substitution. Deliberately the hardest haircut in this set; confidence low.
_demand_record.capture_note: LB-103: pool is addressable-basis; capture_on_addressable 25% base / 50% ceiling (was double-discounted at 10%-on-addressable)

_fare_record.source: Minor Hotels captive gateway — Anantara Uluwatu Benoa marina transfer.

Fare ladder Singapore↔Batam: budget SGD28 (Sindo, HarbourFront→Batam Centre); standard SGD40-43 (BatamFast/Majestic, Batam Centre/Harbour Bay); PREMIUM resort-transfer SGD~73 (BatamFast Tanah Merah→Nongsapura serving Nongsa premium resort zone: Montigo, Turi Beach — real bookings Lemon8 ~SGD73, Rome2Rio Rp430k-650k, DirectFerries from SGD33-35).
_fare_record.method: Premium per-seat anchor = Tanah Merah→Nongsapura (Nongsa resort zone, the corridor's premium endpoint) ~SGD73 x0.78 = USD57. Above the commodity Batam Centre crossing; matches corridor label 'Harbour Bay/Nongsa'.
_fare_record.opex_assignment_flag: CROSS-BORDER: vessel home-ports Singapore (Tanah Merah/HarbourFront), SG crew → assign SINGAPORE origin opex (index 1.0). Destination Indonesia (Batam, index 0.45) cheaper — Indonesian operators (Batam Fast) may home-port Batam-side → reassign. PARENT: decide origin (SG) vs destination (ID). Shortest leg (14nm).

_demand_record.gross_pool_basis: BP Batam (Badan Usaha Pelabuhan) official H1-2024: 4,284,570 total ferry pax at Batam terminals, of which ~2.3M international; 1.75M of those were Singapore-route arrivals+departures (76% of international) -> annualized ~3.5M one-way SG-Batam crossings/yr. Corroboration: BP Batam FY2024 total 8.6M pax all terminals, ~4.8M international, Singapore the dominant route (Tribun Batam citing BP Batam); pre-pandemic SG-Batam served 3.9M pax/yr incl 1.9M foreign tourists (Straits Times). Counts are pax movements at Batam (arrival or departure) = one-way crossings; no x2 applied.

_demand_record.haircut_rationale: Gross is gold-standard on-corridor crossing ridership (port-authority turnstile counts, R3-GOLD-INTL analog; three agreeing T1/T2 sources). Addressable 10% = premium per-seat tier (VIP-class / quality fast-transfer) of a mass S$30-45 crossing market - the corridor's $57 fare row anchors to that tier. R16 note: cross-border corridor; home-port side (SG index 1.00 vs Indonesia ~0.45) is a parent-level opex decision.
_demand_record.capture_note: LB-103: pool is addressable-basis; capture_on_addressable 25% base / 50% ceiling (was double-discounted at 10%-on-addressable)

_pool_override_recal.source: BP Batam SG-route ferry (recovery baseline ~1.2M/yr) × 8% premium capture

_fare_record.source: Only existing boat is the Changi Point->Pulau Ubin bumboat: S$4/pax one-way (NParks official, T1) — budget single-class, no premium tier. No direct Marina Bay->Changi/Ubin boat (14nm long leg is greenfield). Private Ubin boat tours/charters $91-297/group = whole-boat (overclaim). Modeled premium per-seat one-way for the 14nm Marina Bay hop ~$28 (above bumboat budget, below charter).
_fare_record.method: modeled — budget bumboat anchor + greenfield long leg; no premium per-seat scheduled transfer exists

_demand_record.gross_pool_basis: NParks: Pulau Ubin attracts >300,000 visitors/yr; access is BOAT-ONLY via bumboats from Changi Point Ferry Terminal (S$4/pax, ~10 min). 300k visitors x2 = ~600k one-way bumboat crossings/yr (R3-EXCEPTION: boat-only island, arrivals = crossing riders).

sources.label: NParks - Visit Pulau Ubin (bumboat access from Changi Point Ferry Terminal)
Wikipedia (citing NParks) - Pulau Ubin >300,000 visitors annually

_demand_record.haircut_rationale: R3-PIER applied HARD: the 600k real crossings are a ~1nm, S$4 hop from CHANGI POINT, not the modeled 14.2nm Marina Bay leg - the named-origin corridor has zero current ridership. Addressable 5% = the slice plausibly served by a premium direct city-to-Ubin/Changi service (skip the cross-island taxi to Changi). Gross is solid (T2 park authority); addressability on this specific origin is the weak link, hence low-med.

_fare_record.source: Bintan Resort Ferries (BRF, official) Tanah Merah↔Bandar Bentan Telani (Lagoi resort zone), fares eff. 12 Mar 2026: Economy one-way SGD62 adult; EMERALD CLASS one-way SGD89 adult (premium per-seat tier, incl levies). 3rd-party budget listings from SGD53. Charter = 180-270 pax whole vessel (excluded, R1).
_fare_record.method: Premium per-seat anchor = BRF Emerald Class one-way SGD89 x0.78 = USD69. Clean operator-published premium class above Economy — textbook R1 premium ladder point.
_fare_record.opex_assignment_flag: CROSS-BORDER: vessel home-ports Singapore (Tanah Merah), SG crew → assign SINGAPORE origin opex (index 1.0). Destination Indonesia (Riau, index 0.45) far cheaper — if vessel home-ports at BBT/Bintan reassign to Indonesia. PARENT: decide origin (SG) vs destination (ID).

_demand_record.gross_pool_basis: Bintan Resorts (BRC, via TTG Asia interview May-2024): total arrivals 2023 = 500,000 (vs ~1.06M arrivals at Bandar Bentan Telani terminal in 2018, C9 Hotelworks - the pre-covid ceiling). Essentially all Bintan Resorts (Lagoi) guests cross by Bintan Resort Ferries Tanah Merah <-> Bandar Bentan Telani: 500k visitors x2 = ~1.0M one-way crossings/yr. SG-Tanjung Pinang ferry traffic (Sindo/Majestic) is ADDITIVE but not counted (conservative; avoids stretching the resort-corridor pool).
